episode_title: The New Rules of the Climate Economy

real_qa.q: Why does rising fossil fuel price volatility benefit the renewable energy industry?
real_qa.r: When the price of the primary competition for renewable energy goes up, renewable energy looks more attractive. People start to ask themselves whether they should make the switch to cheaper alternatives when fossil fuels are subject to extraordinary price volatility and high prices for long periods of time.
real_qa.requete: fossil fuel prices renewable energy demand

real_qa.q: What percentage of United States greenhouse gas emissions comes from electric power production?
real_qa.r: About a third of the contribution to greenhouse gas emissions in the United States is from electric power production. Another third comes from the transportation sector, including all driving, cars and trucks, shipping, and air travel, with the remainder distributed across building heating, industrial inputs at 20 percent, and agriculture at 10 percent.
real_qa.requete: US greenhouse gas emissions electric power production percentage

real_qa.q: What share of global oil flows through the Straits of Hormuz?
real_qa.r: Twenty percent of the world's oil was flowing through the Straits of Hormuz. Additionally, a significant fraction of the world's liquefied natural gas, about 3 percent, and other critical industrial commodities including fertilizer from the hydrochemical industry flow through those waters.
real_qa.requete: Straits of Hormuz oil LNG percentage global

real_qa.q: How many years of carbon-free electricity does a nuclear power reactor generate?
real_qa.r: Once you build a nuclear reactor, though they are extremely expensive, you have 30 to 50 or more years of essentially zero or very, very low carbon electricity. A thousand megawatts per reactor avoids many of the challenges of renewable energy development because it does not take the same amount of land.
real_qa.requete: nuclear reactor carbon-free electricity years lifespan

real_qa.q: What is the largest single institutional emitter of greenhouse gases in history?
real_qa.r: The largest single institutional emitter of greenhouse gases in the history of the world is the United States Department of Defense. The DOD burns vast amounts of jet fuel, diesel, gasoline, and other fuels, making it the biggest organizational contributor to emissions.
real_qa.requete: United States Department of Defense largest greenhouse gas emitter

real_qa.q: How long will it take to resolve fossil fuel supply disruptions caused by the Iran conflict?
real_qa.r: Even if the Straits of Hormuz opened to prior shipping levels tomorrow, that would not solve the problem for the next probably two years. Facilities that produce oil have been damaged and must be repaired, and other problems related to reserve replenishment will keep prices elevated during that period.
real_qa.requete: Iran conflict oil supply disruption timeline resolution

guest.titre: Professor of Environmental Law and Policy
guest.bio_context: Adam Orford grew up in Alaska and was shaped by the Exxon Valdez oil spill. He spent eight years in private practice at large and boutique law firms representing energy developers, state and local governments, and nonprofits on environmental permitting and climate litigation. He holds a JD, a Master of Public Policy, and a PhD in Energy and Resources, an interdisciplinary program covering climate science, environmental planning, energy economics, and energy engineering.

real_quote: There is a huge amount of systemic inertia in the way that our society is built that doesn't just change overnight. The process of intervening in the systems that keep the lights on is extraordinarily complicated and can be frustratingly slow to change.
